stem: Which biological factor contributes to the high vulnerability of adolescent girls to pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)?

options.text: Lower local immunity and specific biological attributes of the reproductive tract
Faster neurodevelopment in brain regions controlling hygiene
Routine hormonal contraceptive use causing immune suppression
An evolutionary trade-off that prioritises fertility over infection resistance
Reduced exposure to common childhood infections

explanation: Lower local immunity and specific reproductive tract characteristics increase the likelihood of ascending infection and PID in adolescent girls.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because lower local immunity and specific biological features of the reproductive tract make ascending infection and PID more likely.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because neurodevelopment affects behaviour, not the local biological susceptibility of the reproductive tract to PID.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because routine hormonal contraceptive use does not explain the biological vulnerability described here.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because PID vulnerability is due to anatomical and immune factors, not an evolutionary trade-off.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because reduced exposure to childhood infections does not account for the increased reproductive tract susceptibility to PID.

source.hint: Think about the physical and immune characteristics of a developing reproductive system.
